business_model.claim: RLJ is a hotel REIT that owns premium-branded, focused-service and compact full-service hotels. At the latest quarter-end it owned 92 hotel properties with approximately 20,600 rooms.
quotes: We are a self-advised and self-administered Maryland REIT that owns primarily premium-branded, rooms-oriented, high-margin, focused-service and compact full-service hotels located within heart of demand locations.

business_model.claim: Its customers are mostly transient individual business or leisure travelers. Group business using meeting space is a small part of the customer base because most hotels have limited meeting space.
quotes: As a result of this property profile, the majority of our customers are transient in nature.
Given the limited meeting space at the majority of our hotels, group business that utilizes meeting space represents a small component of our customer base.

business_model.claim: The company sells three revenue lines. In the latest quarter, total revenues were 354,476, made up of room revenue of 288,366, food and beverage revenue of 38,183 and other revenue of 27,927 (table in thousands of dollars).
Room revenue is the dominant line, at approximately 81.0% of total revenues in the prior full year, and it depends on occupancy, pricing and the supply of rooms.
quotes: Room revenue comprised approximately 81.0% of our total revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025, and it is dictated by demand (as measured by Occupancy), pricing (as measured by ADR) and our available supply of hotel rooms.

business_model.claim: RLJ owns hotels through an operating partnership, leases almost all of them to taxable REIT subsidiaries (91 of 92), and hires independent managers to run them. The company receives monthly cash equal to hotel-level sales less hotel-level operating expenses.
quotes: We lease 91 of the 92 hotel properties to our TRSs, of which we own a controlling financial interest.
We generally receive a cash distribution from the management companies on a monthly basis, which reflects hotel-level sales less hotel-level operating expenses.

business_model.basis: inferred from the stated use of Hotel EBITDA and the segment note reference; segment names are not in the evidence
business_model.claim: Management assesses performance at the hotel level using Hotel EBITDA, and the filing points to a segment information note. The extracts do not name any reporting segments.
quotes: In addition, we use Hotel EBITDA, a non-GAAP financial measure, to assess operating performance.

business_model.claim: Room revenue is driven by occupancy and ADR, which together make RevPAR. In the latest quarter, comparable RevPAR was $153.36, up 9.7%, with ADR of $203.35 and occupancy of 75.4%.
quotes: RevPAR is the product of ADR and Occupancy.
Comparable RevPAR of $153.36, an increase of 9.7% over the prior year

business_model.claim: Food and beverage revenue depends on occupancy and the type of guest, with group business generating more catering revenue. Other revenue (parking, resort fees, gift shop sales) depends on occupancy and the nature of the hotel.
quotes: Other revenue — Occupancy and the nature of the hotel property are the main drivers of other ancillary revenue, such as parking fees, resort fees, gift shop sales and other guest service fees.

business_model.claim: Property operating expenses (room, food and beverage, management and franchise fees, other) were 238,398 in the latest quarter versus 223,364 a year earlier (table in thousands). Management and franchise fees were 26,826 of that. Most variable costs, including labor, move with occupancy, while base management fees are a percentage of gross hotel revenues.
quotes: Most categories of variable operating expenses, including labor costs, fluctuate with changes in Occupancy.
A base management fee is computed as a percentage of gross hotel revenues.

business_model.claim: ADR changes affect margins more than occupancy changes because they have only a limited effect on variable operating costs.
quotes: Changes in ADR typically have a greater impact on operating margins and profitability as they only have a limited effect on variable operating costs.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; the combination into a cost structure is inferred
business_model.claim: Below the hotel level, costs include depreciation and amortization of 47,723, property tax, insurance and other of 24,636, general and administrative expense of 13,325, and interest expense of 29,831 versus 28,309 a year earlier (table in thousands). Debt, net was 2,196,326 at the latest balance sheet date. After swaps, 69.2% of payments were fixed or effectively fixed at the prior year-end.
quotes: After taking into consideration the effect of interest rate swaps, 69.2% of our payments are fixed or effectively fixed.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item; the mechanism is partly inferred
business_model.claim: Revenue growth showed operating leverage in the latest quarter. Comparable Hotel Revenue rose 9.1% and Comparable Hotel EBITDA rose 17.5%, lifting the margin to 26.5%, up 190 basis points.
quotes: allowed us to expand margins and grow Hotel EBITDA at nearly twice the pace of revenues

business_model.claim: Demand drivers are the economy, business and leisure travel, and urban market conditions. Management attributes the latest quarter's gains to business travel, leisure and group demand. Revenue was weaker in the prior full year, when comparable RevPAR fell to $143.43 from $145.99 on lower international, government, corporate and group travel.
quotes: business travel leading the way alongside sustained strength in leisure and group

business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated in three franchise brand families. At the prior year-end, 83 of 93 hotels were Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt brands, and both brand and manager relationships can affect results.
quotes: 83 of the 93 hotel properties that we owned as of December 31, 2025 were affiliated with brands owned by Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt.

business_model.claim: The company also recycles capital by selling hotels. A combined sales price of approximately $123.2 million was reported for 2026 sales, and hotel properties held for sale of 105,847 appear on the balance sheet (table in thousands).
quotes: The sale of eight hotel properties in two separate transactions for a combined sales price of approximately $123.2 million.

business_model.claim: Hotel revenue turns into cash from operations of 209,767 over nine months (table in thousands). The cash funds property improvements of 76,171, common distributions of 68,859 and preferred distributions of 18,836. The REIT rules require distributing at least 90% of REIT taxable income, which limits how much capital spending can come from operating cash.
quotes: We may not be able to fund the capital improvements to our hotel properties or acquisitions solely from the cash provided from our operating activities because we must distribute annually at least 90% of our REIT taxable income to shareholders in order to maintain our qualification as a REIT.

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal, with northeastern hotels weaker in winter and Florida hotels stronger in early months of the year, which causes quarterly fluctuations.
quotes: The lodging industry is seasonal in nature, which can cause quarterly fluctuations in our revenues.

business_model.claim: Management's full-year outlook is built on these drivers, with comparable RevPAR growth of +5.75% to +6.25% and Adjusted EBITDA of $352M to $358M.

competitive_position.claim: RLJ positions itself as an owner of premium-branded, focused-service and compact full-service hotels in urban demand locations. The portfolio was 93 hotels with approximately 20,800 rooms in 23 states and DC at year-end 2025, and 92 hotels with approximately 20,600 rooms at September 30, 2026.
quotes: We are a self-advised and self-administered Maryland real estate investment trust that owns primarily premium-branded, rooms-oriented, high-margin, focused-service and compact full-service hotels located within heart of demand locations.
As of September 30, 2026, we owned 92 hotel properties with approximately 20,600 rooms, located in 23 states and the District of Columbia.

competitive_position.claim: Scale and brand affiliation are part of the position. Approximately 89.3% of hotels operate under Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt relationships, and the company says it is one of the largest U.S. publicly-traded lodging REITs by hotel and room count.
quotes: Our hotel properties operate under industry-leading, premium brands, with approximately 89.3% of our hotel properties operating under existing relationships with Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt.
We are one of the largest U.S. publicly-traded lodging REITs in terms of both number of hotels and number of rooms.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item (press release)
competitive_position.claim: Q3 2026 operating performance was strong. Comparable RevPAR was $153.36, up 9.7%, with ADR of $203.35 (up 6.4%) and occupancy of 75.4% against 73.1%. Management says this outpaced the industry and cites business travel, leisure and group demand benefiting urban markets.
quotes: Comparable RevPAR of $153.36, an increase of 9.7% over the prior year
As a result, we achieved robust RevPAR growth of 9.7%, outpacing the industry, driven by increases in both demand and rate.

competitive_position.claim: Hotel-level profitability improved in Q3 2026. Comparable Hotel EBITDA Margin was 26.5%, up 190 basis points, and management says Hotel EBITDA grew at nearly twice the pace of revenues.
quotes: Comparable Hotel EBITDA Margin of 26.5%, an increase of 190 basis points over the prior year
allowed us to expand margins and grow Hotel EBITDA at nearly twice the pace of revenues,”

competitive_position.claim: The position was weaker in 2025. Comparable RevPAR fell to $143.43 from $145.99 and occupancy to 71.6% from 72.7%. Management attributed the room revenue decline to lower international, government, corporate and group travel.
quotes: The decrease in room revenue from the comparable properties was primarily due to a decrease in international, government, corporate and group travel.

competitive_position.claim: Newly converted and renovated hotels are adding non-room revenue. Q3 food and beverage revenue was 38,183 (table in thousands) against 36,884, and other revenue was 27,927 against 25,794. Management says the ramp of conversions and renovations added momentum.
quotes: The ramp of our conversions and renovations provided additional momentum, which contributed to continued growth in non-room revenues.

competitive_position.claim: Management raised its full-year 2026 outlook, with comparable RevPAR growth guided at +5.75% to +6.25%. It cites strong preliminary October results, and the outlook excludes seven Chicago Midway assets sold after the third quarter.
quotes: Given our third quarter outperformance, strong preliminary results for October, and our expectation that positive trends will carry into the remainder of the year, we are raising our full-year guidance.
Comparable RevPAR and Hotel EBITDA outlooks exclude the seven Chicago Midway assets sold subsequent to the third quarter.

competitive_position.claim: The company is recycling capital and reshaping its portfolio. Management lists the sale of eight hotels for approximately $123.2 million, and the balance sheet shows hotel properties held for sale of 105,847 (table in thousands) at Sep 30, 2026.
quotes: The sale of eight hotel properties in two separate transactions for a combined sales price of approximately $123.2 million.

competitive_position.claim: The balance sheet is a competitive constraint. Debt, net was 2,196,326 (table in thousands) at Sep 30, 2026 against 2,197,218 at Dec 31, 2025, and the 10-K names debt as a source of competitive disadvantage. The 2026 Refinancing Transactions repaid the 2026 Senior Notes at maturity and recast the $600.0 million Revolver.
quotes: At December 31, 2025, we had approximately $2.2 billion of debt outstanding, which could materially and adversely affect our operating performance and put us at a competitive disadvantage.
After taking into consideration the effect of interest rate swaps, 69.2% of our payments are fixed or effectively fixed.

competitive_position.claim: Concentration in a few markets exposes the company to local conditions. Northern California, Southern California, South Florida, Chicago and Houston accounted for 13.4%, 11.1%, 9.1%, 6.5% and 5.8% of rooms available in 2025.
quotes: Our hotels located in the Northern California, Southern California, South Florida, Chicago, Illinois, and Houston, Texas metropolitan areas accounted for approximately 13.4%, 11.1%, 9.1%, 6.5% and 5.8%, respectively, of our total number of rooms available for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025.

competitive_position.claim: Dependence on third-party managers is a named threat. All hotels have individual management agreements, 26 with Aimbridge and 21 with Hilton, and the company has limited ability to control manager employee costs.
quotes: We retain independent third-party hotel managers to operate our hotel properties pursuant to management agreements.
We have limited ability (or in some cases, no ability) to control cost increases related to our independent managers' employees.

competitive_position.claim: Brand concentration is a named threat, with 83 of 93 hotels affiliated with Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt brands. Damage to those brands or a deteriorated relationship could lead to loss of franchise licenses.
quotes: 83 of the 93 hotel properties that we owned as of December 31, 2025 were affiliated with brands owned by Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt.

competitive_position.claim: Competition from other hotels and non-traditional lodging is a named threat. Competitors with lower-rate operating models could take occupancy and pressure ADR.
quotes: Our competitors may have an operating model that enables them to offer accommodations at lower rates than we can, which could result in our competitors increasing their Occupancy at our expense and adversely affecting our ADRs.
